children: memorandums of understanding with Brazilian energy company Eneva and WESCA to pursue oil ​and gas development opportunities in Venezuela; financial terms were not disclosed.

said it will build upon its existing relationship with Eneva, Brazil's largest private natural gas operator, to identify and pursue development opportunities in Venezuela, and under a separate MoU, it will support WESCA with field evaluation and ​development planning, building on their existing work in ​reservoir analysis, digital technologies, and subsurface interpretation.

Interest in Venezuela has ramped up ‌since the U.S. capture of former President Maduro in January, and companies with existing positions in the country, as well ​as those seeking new opportunities, are negotiating ⁠or finalizing agreements that could expand production and improve infrastructure.

Recently, Continental ​Resources signed MoUs with ​Venezuela's state ⁠oil company PDVSA seeking to further operate and develop the Orinoco Belt, Chevron said it plans to spend $7B ⁠through its Venezuela joint ventures, and Exxon reportedly is in talks to return to the country.
